note: He is close to a perfect programme fit and clearly outside the stated ICP, which is the finding. On the programme side he is exactly right: 17 years of training, a decade of CrossFit, currently fit at 5'10" and 183 lb, self-directed, and explicitly wanting good-to-great rather than rescue — the opposite of the '50 pounds overweight and hates working out' exclusion. On the commercial side he fails both money criteria. He is a unionised schoolteacher, not a business owner or physician, with about USD 1,400 of cash, no savings and no investments, a monthly surplus in the hundreds, and a daughter entering her senior year with known costs coming. He also inverts the neglected_health criterion: health is the one area of his life he has never neglected — it is the area he has invested in most consistently for 17 years, while income is the constraint. The stated ICP assumes a successful professional whose training has slipped; Mike is a fit man whose finances are tight, and the sale only stayed alive by moving him onto a $30,000 line of credit.
